title: Photosynthetic electron transport and plastid redox

nodes.label: Plastocyanin (PETE1/2)
nodes.rationale: A mononuclear Cu(II)/Cu(I) centre performing one-electron transfer, so formally paramagnetic in the oxidised state.
nodes.caveat: Deliberately classed as spin_relaxation_modulated rather than as a radical-pair partner. A single copper centre relaxes fast and has no correlated partner, so coherent singlet-triplet mixing is not available here; only a relaxation-based effect could be argued, and none has been shown.

nodes.label: Photosystem II
nodes.rationale: The QA/QB sites hold a kinetically stabilised plastosemiquinone, and PSII is a major singlet-oxygen source under excess light. Both are one-electron chemistry in a defined pocket, which is the setting a radical-pair argument needs.
nodes.caveat: PSII's dominant ROS species is singlet oxygen from the P680 triplet, not superoxide. Triplet chlorophyll formation is itself spin chemistry, so a field effect here would be more plausible than at most nodes — but it is also a route the review does not develop, and no measurement exists.

nodes.label: Plastosemiquinone (PQ·−)
nodes.rationale: The plastid counterpart of ubisemiquinone, and the same argument applies: a protein-bound organic radical with a measurable lifetime is the most credible site for field-dependent branching in the chain.

nodes.label: Cytochrome b6f Rieske [2Fe-2S] (PETC)
nodes.rationale: Structurally and mechanistically the plastid twin of the mitochondrial Rieske centre (QBO:RIESKE_FES), with the same bifurcated Q-cycle chemistry. The review treats both as the same class of candidate target.

nodes.label: Cytochrome b6 / f hemes (PETA, PETB)
nodes.rationale: One-electron heme carriers, paramagnetic in the ferric state, adjacent to the semiquinone-generating Q cycle.

nodes.label: Photosystem I Fe/S centres (FX, FA, FB)
nodes.rationale: PSI is the strongest structural case in the whole atlas. Charge separation at P700 produces a genuine spin-correlated radical pair (P700·+ A1·−), which is the textbook example of the species the radical-pair mechanism describes — it is studied by exactly that formalism in photosynthesis spectroscopy. Three [4Fe-4S] clusters then carry the electron onward.
nodes.caveat: The P700·+ A1·− pair is extremely short-lived, and the well-characterised magnetic-field effects on it are seen in isolated preparations at fields far above geomagnetic. Structural plausibility is high; relevance at 50 uT is not established.

evidence.claim: The geomagnetic field is required for normal lima bean photosynthesis, PSI/LHCI content and ROS production; near-null field conditions altered photosynthetic electron transport.

nodes.label: Ferredoxin (FD1, FD2)
nodes.rationale: The distribution hub of plastid reducing power. A perturbation here reaches carbon fixation, nitrogen and sulfur assimilation and redox regulation at once, which is why the review nominates ferredoxin biogenesis specifically.

evidence.claim: Geomagnetic field conditions modulate iron-sulfur interplay in Arabidopsis, particularly under combined iron and sulfur deficiency.

nodes.label: Ferredoxin-NADP+ reductase (FNR1, FNR2)
nodes.rationale: FNR necessarily transits a flavin semiquinone: it is the step that converts one-electron chemistry into two-electron chemistry, so a half-reduced flavin is obligatory rather than incidental. That makes it the plastid's clearest analogue of the cryptochrome flavin.

nodes.label: Plastid superoxide / H2O2
nodes.rationale: As in the mitochondrion, the amplifier rather than the mechanism: threshold behaviour converts a small change in electron branching into a signal.

evidence.claim: Reactive oxygen species production differed between geomagnetic and near-null field conditions in lima bean.
Near-null magnetic field alters ROS-associated transcriptomic and metabolomic programmes in Arabidopsis.
